architecture_methodology_note: Pfizer Global Supply (PGS) structures its pharmaceutical and biopharma operations around GxP-regulated end-to-end pillars documented in Pfizer's 10-K & PGS disclosures: Commercial & Clinical Trial Demand Planning (01), Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) & Sterile Excipient Sourcing (02), cGMP Biopharma Manufacturing & Batch Release (03), GDP Cold/Ultra-Cold Distribution (04), Serialized DSCSA/EU-FMD Healthcare Delivery (05), and Regulated Reverse/Expiry Governance (06).

terminology_highlights: API (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient) — The biologically active component of a drug product, synthesized in specialized chemical or biological facilities.
Cold Chain — A temperature-controlled supply chain essential for preserving the efficacy of biologics and mRNA vaccines (e.g., ultra-low temperature freezers and dry ice shippers).
CMO / CDMO — Contract (Development and) Manufacturing Organizations used to supplement internal production capacity for drug substance or drug product.
Serialization — The process of assigning a unique, traceable serial number to each saleable unit of prescription drugs to prevent counterfeiting and ensure compliance.
